Cyclohexene reacts with diiodoketene in a [2+2] cycloaddition to form the cyclobutanone derivative 8,8-diiodobicyclo[4.2.0]octan-7-one. Diiodoketene is named 2,2-diiodoethen-1-one. The alternative, 4,4-diiodocyclobut-2-en-1-one, would ring-open to a vinyl ketene and give a different product. For the diene reactivity sequence in Diels–Alder reactions: cyclopenta-1,3-diene (3) is locked in the s-cis conformation and is the most reactive; 2,3-dimethylbuta-1,3-diene (1) has electron-donating methyl groups and can adopt the s-cis form easily; (2E,4E)-hexa-2,4-diene (2) must overcome steric interactions to achieve s-cis; (2Z,4Z)-hexa-2,4-diene (4) suffers severe steric hindrance in the s-cis conformation and is the least reactive. The order from most to least reactive is 3 > 1 > 2 > 4.

4. (2Z,4Z)-hexa-2,4-diene: Z,Z isomer. It is forced to be s-cis or at least can easily adopt s-cis, but has steric hindrance. Typically, (Z,Z)-dienes are more reactive than E,E because they are already in or near the s-cis conformation. But cyclopentadiene is even more reactive because it's locked in s-cis and has no steric hindrance to adopting planar structure.

Reactivity order for Diels-Alder dienes: cyclic s-cis locked dienes > acyclic dienes with s-cis conformation accessible > acyclic dienes with s-trans preference. Electron-donating groups increase reactivity. Steric hindrance can decrease reactivity.
